title: US Indicts Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and Nine Officials on Drug Trafficking Charges, Triggering Federal Crisis
detail: US federal prosecutors charged Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other state officials and police commanders with drug trafficking links to the Sinaloa Cartel, including alleged facilitation of the governor's 2021 gubernatorial campaign through cartel-sponsored kidnapping and ballot fraud. The indictment — announced days after the CIA unauthorized incident in Chihuahua — represents the most dramatic US legal action against a sitting Mexican state governor in modern history. President Sheinbaum publicly rejected any extradition absent 'irrefutable evidence,' invoking Mexico's sovereignty and constitutional processes. She stated Mexico would investigate the charges through its own institutions. The Sheinbaum government walked a careful line: declining to immediately remove or distance itself from Rocha Moya while signaling zero tolerance for cartel infiltration. CSIS analysts noted the indictment came amid heightened US pressure in the USMCA renegotiation period and days before the first formal USMCA Joint Review round. Critics questioned the timing, suggesting political motivation given the trade negotiations. The US action intensified an already acute sovereignty dispute stemming from the CIA Chihuahua incident six days earlier.

media.caption: US indicts Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya on drug trafficking charges, creating major US-Mexico diplomatic crisis

title: Culiacán Labor Leader Homar Salas Gastélum Shot Dead on Eve of May Day
detail: Homar Salas Gastélum, the elected leader of the Union of Workers at the Service of the City of Culiacán (STASAC), was shot and killed at his home in Culiacán, Sinaloa, one day before International Workers' Day. Peace Brigades International (PBI) documented the killing as part of a regional pattern of targeted attacks against labor leaders and human rights defenders across Mexico, Colombia, Honduras, and Guatemala coinciding with May 1 demonstrations. Salas Gastélum had been a vocal advocate for municipal workers' rights and was known for resisting informal pressure from organized crime-affiliated interests in Culiacán's labor sector. His assassination came at a moment of acute instability in Sinaloa: the day coincided with the announcement of the US federal indictment of Governor Rubén Rocha Moya on drug trafficking charges. Mexico's labor movement has faced a sustained campaign of targeted killings under the Sheinbaum administration, with the National Federation of Independent Unions (FENSIL) documenting 14 labor leader killings in the first six months of 2026. Mexico's criminal impunity rate of 97% means the vast majority of such killings go unprosecuted.

media.caption: Culiacán labor leader Homar Salas Gastélum killed on May Day eve; part of broader pattern of violence against labor rights defenders
